mappings.note: What the old man actually said is quoted in the text; retrieval, LO-1, while why it stung her pride would be LO-2.
Meaning of 'wistfully' as used in the line. Vocabulary, C-E1.1.
Valliammai is named in the opening sentence; retrieval, LO-1.
Her wish to ride the bus is stated; retrieval, LO-1.
Her envy of friends' bus stories is stated; retrieval, LO-1.
The reason she stood - she could not see over the blind - is stated; retrieval, LO-1.
Part i checks which statement the extract supports (LO-1); the longer part explains why the bus held such a pull for a girl confined to her street, which is character in context (LO-2).
Three parts retrieve her pastime and why she had no playmates (LO-1); the last asks for a substitute for 'friends', a vocabulary item (C-E1.1).
Sixty paise for the return trip is a stated figure; retrieval, LO-1.
Asks what her wistful staring reveals - her longing to ride the bus. An inference about the character, LO-2, not a lifted fact.
Interprets the figurative line about a wish that 'crept into her head and grew there'. Inferring and interpreting, C-E1.1.
Asks what her retort plus her laughter shows about her - mixed irritation and amusement. Character inference, LO-2.
Fill-in of the bus as her source of unending joy; a stated fact, LO-1. (The row's marked option and its printed answer disagree, so the key needs review.)

A speaking task: mimic people who have spoken to you, with your own replies. Expression with attention to voice and tone, C-E1.2.
Asks for the learner's concerns about road safety and their own proposals. Opinion with reasons, C-E1.2.
Authorship of the lesson. Knowledge about the work itself, which no LO covers, so C-E1.4.
